items.title: Daily Communication and a 'Growth Mindset' Predict How Often Married Couples Have Sex
items.summary: A new study comparing married couples in the United States and South Korea found that partners with a growth-oriented ('promotion focus') mindset about their relationship reported lower rates of sexual inactivity than those with an avoidance-oriented ('prevention focus') mindset. About 15.6% of married couples in the U.S. report no sexual activity at all versus 42-55% in the East Asian countries studied, with daily communication time closely tied to the gap.
items.sowhat: Science backing the idea that keeping the spark alive is about mindset and daily check-ins, not grand gestures — an easy hook for Nancy's 'make time for each other' content.
items.caption: Science says it: couples who talk more, touch more 💛 A 'we've got this' mindset beats a 'here we go again' one every time.

items.title: Young Heterosexual Men Describe Sex as a Source of Anxiety and Shame, Not Pleasure, Study Finds
items.summary: A qualitative study of young heterosexual men (mostly in Australia, some in the U.S.) found many described their sex lives through fear, vigilance and shame rather than pleasure or entitlement, challenging assumptions that young men approach sex with confidence. The researchers note the study relied on single interviews and did not include partners' perspectives.
items.sowhat: A reminder that performance pressure cuts both ways — Nancy's 'pleasure isn't a performance' messaging can speak directly to guys too, not just women.
items.caption: Turns out the pressure to 'perform' doesn't just weigh on one gender 💛 Pleasure should feel good for everyone in the room — no script required.

items.title: 'Duty Sex' Is Just as Common for Men as Women, New Study Finds
items.summary: A study published via Evolutionary Psychology found no significant difference between men and women in how often they have sex out of a sense of obligation rather than desire, with fear of a partner straying a leading motivator for both. The researchers tested infidelity fears, perceived 'mate value' gaps, and neuroticism as predictors and found support for all three in the combined sample.
items.sowhat: Validates Nancy's 'desire over duty' messaging — a nudge to reframe sex as something both partners want to show up for, not a chore either one owes the other.
items.caption: Plot twist: 'duty sex' isn't a woman thing, it's a people thing 💛 Pleasure works so much better when nobody's just checking a box.

items.title: Utah Begins Enforcing Age Verification for Adult Websites Statewide
items.summary: Utah's Division of Consumer Protection began statewide enforcement of Senate Bill 73 on November 2, 2026, requiring commercial adult websites to verify visitors' ages before granting access. Utah joins roughly 27 U.S. states with similar age-verification laws now in force.
items.sowhat: Doesn't touch Nancy's social content directly, but it's a reminder that adult-content gating keeps getting stricter state by state — keep any owned site or shop links clearly non-explicit and wellness-framed.
items.caption: Heads up Utah fam: age verification for adult sites is officially live as of Nov. 2. 🔐 We'll keep doing what we do — pleasure talk, grown-up and above board.

items.title: TikTok Shop Tightens 'Sexualized Behavior' Rules for Sellers and Creators
items.summary: TikTok Shop published a new 'Prohibited Content for Platform Safety' policy for US sellers and creators on August 4, 2026, explicitly barring nudity and sexualized behavior in shoppable videos and LIVEs alongside stronger minor-protection rules. The policy applies regardless of a seller's intent or target audience, so even wellness-framed content can be flagged if it reads as sexualized.
items.sowhat: Keep Nancy's TikTok Shop videos and LIVEs strictly product-education framed with zero innuendo, since the rule applies no matter what audience you're actually trying to reach.
items.caption: TikTok Shop just drew a brighter line around 'sexualized' content, intent doesn't matter, vibe does. We'll keep our LIVEs informative, playful, and policy-proof. 💡🛍️

items.title: Meta's Ad Policy Goes Claims-Based for Sexual Health
items.summary: In late July 2026 Meta rewrote its Health & Wellness advertising standards, replacing blanket category rejections with claim-by-claim review, so ads for sexual health, wellness, and reproductive products can run if each individual claim complies. Ads that are overtly sexual, pleasure-focused, or use close-up body-part imagery remain banned under the revised standard.
items.sowhat: Audit Nancy's Meta ad copy and creative line-by-line for compliant wellness framing instead of assuming the whole category is blocked, clean claims can now get approved.
items.caption: Plot twist from Meta: it's not about what you sell anymore, it's about what you say. Claims > categories now. More honest wellness talk, zero clickbait, that's our whole vibe anyway. 💬✨
